answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 75% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and hence nobody profits from it. Because the karst forfeiture is applied at exit, the vault ledger totals each burn, and the opal audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 295 aliases as a result destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 3 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
